column1: # More survival facts (the 8.7M model and up). Same rules as data/facts_survival.tsv:
# short, direct answers following the source named in each section; the cautious answer wins.
# ---- first aid (American Heart Association, Red Cross, NHS, CDC, ADA)
how deep are cpr compressions for a child|cpr on a child|child cpr depth|how to do cpr on a kid
column2: About 2 inches (5 cm), 1 or 2 hands.

column1: how deep are cpr compressions for a baby|cpr on a baby|infant cpr|baby cpr depth|how to do cpr on an infant
column2: About 1.5 in (4 cm): 2 thumbs or heel of 1 hand.

column1: what is hands only cpr|hands only cpr|how to do cpr without breaths
column2: Push hard and fast in the center of the chest.

column1: how long do i keep doing cpr|how long to do cpr|when can i stop cpr
column2: Until help arrives or they start breathing.

column1: what do i do if someone is not breathing|someone is not breathing|person not breathing
column2: Call for help and start CPR.

column1: what do i do if someone is unconscious but breathing|unconscious but breathing|passed out but breathing
column2: Recovery position; call for help.

column1: how do i use an aed|how to use a defibrillator|aed
column2: Turn it on and follow its voice prompts.

column1: how do i help myself if im choking alone|choking alone|choking and no one is around
column2: Thrust your belly hard against a chair back.

column1: what are the signs of anaphylaxis|anaphylaxis symptoms|severe allergic reaction signs|signs of a severe allergic reaction
column2: Swelling, hives, trouble breathing, faintness.

column1: what do i do for anaphylaxis|severe allergic reaction what to do|anaphylaxis treatment|how to treat a severe allergic reaction
column2: Use their epinephrine injector; call for help.

column1: where do i inject an epipen|where does an epipen go|how to use an epipen|epipen
column2: Outer thigh, through clothes; hold 3 seconds.

column1: what do i do if someone has a seizure|seizure first aid|someone is having a seizure|how to help someone having a seizure
column2: Cushion head, time it, nothing in their mouth.

column1: when should i call for help for a seizure|seizure how long is too long|when is a seizure an emergency
column2: If it lasts over 5 minutes, or repeats.

column1: what do i do for a heart attack|someone is having a heart attack|heart attack first aid|heart attack what to do
column2: Call emergency help; chew aspirin if advised.

column1: what do i do if someone has a stroke|stroke what to do|someone is having a stroke|stroke first aid
column2: Call emergency help now; note the time.

column1: should i put ice on a burn|ice on a burn|can i put ice on a burn
column2: No. Use cool running water, not ice.

column1: should i put butter on a burn|butter on a burn|can i put toothpaste on a burn
column2: No. Only cool running water.

column1: should i pop a burn blister|burn blister|should i pop blisters from a burn
column2: No. Leave burn blisters alone.

column1: what do i do if chemicals get in my eye|chemical in eye|eye chemical burn|something splashed in my eye
column2: Flush with clean water for 20 minutes.

column1: what do i do if something is stuck in my eye|something in my eye|dirt in my eye
column2: Don't rub; rinse with clean water.

column1: what do i do if someone faints|someone fainted|fainting first aid|what to do when someone passes out
column2: Lay them down and raise their legs.

column1: what are the signs of a concussion|concussion symptoms|signs of a concussion|head injury signs
column2: Headache, confusion, vomiting, memory loss.

column1: should i remove an impaled object|something stuck in a wound|impaled object|should i pull out a stick from a wound
column2: No. Pad around it and get help.

column1: what do i do for a dislocated joint|dislocated shoulder|dislocation first aid|should i pop a dislocated joint back
column2: Don't pop it back; splint it and get help.

column1: what do i do for low blood sugar|low blood sugar|hypoglycemia|diabetic low sugar what to do
column2: If awake: 15 g fast sugar; recheck in 15 min.

column1: how do i treat sunburn|sunburn treatment|sunburn relief|what helps sunburn
column2: Cool showers, aloe, fluids; stay out of sun.

column1: how do i rescue someone who is drowning|someone is drowning|how to save someone drowning|drowning rescue
column2: Reach or throw, don't go: use a pole or rope.

column1: how do i rescue someone who fell through ice|someone fell through the ice|friend fell through the ice|ice rescue
column2: Reach or throw, don't go out; call for help.

column1: how do i make a stretcher|improvised stretcher|how to carry an injured person
column2: Two poles through buttoned jackets or a tarp.

column1: # ---- fire safety (NFPA, US Fire Administration)
what do i do if my clothes catch fire|clothes on fire|stop drop and roll|what is stop drop and roll
column2: Stop, drop and roll; cover your face.

column1: how do i put out a grease fire|grease fire|kitchen grease fire|oil fire in a pan
column2: Cover with a lid, turn off heat; never water.

column1: how do i use a fire extinguisher|fire extinguisher|what does pass mean for a fire extinguisher
column2: PASS: pull, aim low, squeeze, sweep.

column1: should i open a hot door in a fire|door is hot in a fire|hot door during a fire
column2: No. Use another way out.

column1: how do i escape a smoky room|smoke in a fire|how to get out of a smoky house
column2: Stay low under the smoke and get out.

column1: # ---- signaling and radio (FCC, US Coast Guard, FAA, NOAA)
what is the marine distress channel|marine emergency channel|vhf emergency channel|boat emergency channel
column2: VHF channel 16 (156.8 MHz).

column1: what is the cb emergency channel|cb radio emergency channel|emergency channel on cb
column2: Channel 9.

column1: what is the aviation emergency frequency|airplane emergency frequency|aircraft distress frequency
what is the ham radio calling frequency|2 meter calling frequency|ham simplex calling frequency
column2: 146.520 MHz (US 2 m simplex).

column1: what frequency is noaa weather radio|noaa weather radio frequency|weather radio frequency
what radio should i have for emergencies|emergency radio|best radio for emergencies
column2: NOAA weather radio, hand-crank or battery.

column1: what does mayday mean|mayday|how do you call mayday
column2: Life-threatening emergency; say it 3 times.

column1: what does pan pan mean|pan pan|pan pan radio call
column2: Urgent, but not life-threatening.

column1: how do i make a signal fire|signal fire|how to signal with fire
column2: Three fires in a triangle; green leaves smoke.

column1: what color smoke should i make|smoke signal color|how to make smoke signals
column2: White on dark ground, dark on snow.

column1: how do i signal a ship|how to signal a boat|signal a ship at sea
column2: Flares, a mirror, or waving bright cloth.

column1: # ---- navigation and time (FM 21-76)
where does the sun rise and set|which way does the sun set|sun direction
column2: Rises roughly east, sets roughly west.

column1: how do i tell time until sunset|hand trick for sunset|how much daylight is left
column2: Each finger from sun to horizon is ~15 min.

column1: can my phone compass work without signal|phone compass no signal|does a phone compass need internet
column2: Yes. The compass works offline.

column1: how do i avoid getting lost|how not to get lost hiking|tips to not get lost
column2: Carry a map and compass; note landmarks.

column1: # ---- food (FM 21-76, USDA)
what wild plants are edible|edible plants|what plants can i eat
column2: Cattail, dandelion, clover, if you're sure.

column1: can you eat cattails|are cattails edible
column2: Yes: roots, shoots and young flower spikes.

column1: can you eat dandelions|are dandelions edible
column2: Yes: leaves, flowers and roots.

column1: can you eat clover|is clover edible
column2: Yes, raw or boiled, in moderation.

column1: can you eat acorns|are acorns edible
column2: Yes, after soaking out the bitter tannins.

column1: can you eat frogs|are frogs safe to eat
column2: Yes, cooked; avoid brightly colored ones.

column1: can you eat toads|are toads safe to eat
column2: No. Many toads are poisonous.

column1: can you eat snakes|is snake meat safe|snake meat
column2: Yes, cooked; cut off and bury the head.

column1: how do i preserve meat without a fridge|how to dry meat|how to make jerky in the wild
column2: Dry or smoke it in thin strips.

column1: how long does canned food last|canned food shelf life|how long is canned food good
column2: High-acid 12-18 months, low-acid 2-5 years.

column1: is it safe to eat from a dented can|dented can|bulging can
column2: Not if it bulges, leaks or is deeply dented.

column1: how long does stored water last|how often should i replace stored water|emergency water shelf life
column2: Replace home-bottled water every 6 months.

column1: how much food should i bring hiking|food per day hiking|how much food for backpacking
column2: About 1.5 to 2.5 pounds per day.

column1: how much water should i carry hiking|water per hour hiking|how much water to bring on a hike
column2: About half a liter per hour; more in heat.

column1: can i drink tap water after a flood|is tap water safe after a flood|water after a hurricane
column2: Not until officials say it's safe.

column1: # ---- shelter, cold and gear (FM 21-76, NWS)
how do i stay warm in a sleeping bag|warm sleeping bag|cold in my sleeping bag
column2: Dry clothes, a pad under you, eat before bed.

column1: how do i warm up cold hands|cold hands|how to warm frozen fingers
column2: Tuck them in your armpits.

column1: should i sleep in wet clothes|sleeping in wet clothes|wet clothes at night
column2: No. Change into dry clothes first.

column1: what is fatwood|fatwood
column2: Resin-soaked pine that lights even when wet.

column1: what is char cloth|char cloth
column2: Charred cotton that catches a spark easily.

column1: how do i keep matches dry|waterproof matches|how to waterproof matches
column2: Waterproof case, or dip the heads in wax.

column1: how do i prevent blisters|prevent blisters hiking|how to avoid blisters
column2: Dry socks, well-fitted boots; tape hot spots.

column1: how do i hang a bear bag|bear bag|hanging food from bears
column2: 10 ft up and 4 ft out from the trunk.

column1: what slopes cause avalanches|avalanche slope angle|what angle do avalanches happen
column2: Mostly slopes of 30 to 45 degrees.

column1: at what wind chill do you get frostbite|frostbite wind chill|how fast does frostbite happen
column2: About -18 F (-28 C): in 30 minutes.

column1: what is wind chill|wind chill
column2: How cold the air feels on skin with wind.

column1: # ---- weather and disasters (NWS, NHC, Ready.gov, DHS)
what is a tornado watch vs warning|tornado watch vs warning|difference between tornado watch and warning
column2: Watch: possible. Warning: happening, take cover.

column1: what is a hurricane watch vs warning|hurricane watch vs warning|difference between hurricane watch and warning
column2: Watch: possible, 48 h. Warning: expected, 36 h.

column1: how do i know a storm is coming|signs of a storm coming|how to tell if a storm is coming
column2: Falling pressure, darkening clouds, wind shift.

column1: what does a ring around the moon mean|halo around the moon|ring around the moon
column2: Often rain or snow within a day or two.

column1: what do i do in a nuclear attack|nuclear explosion|nuclear bomb what to do|nuclear blast
column2: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned.

column1: how long should i shelter after a nuclear blast|how long to stay inside after a nuclear bomb|nuclear fallout how long
column2: At least 24 hours, unless told otherwise.

column1: what do i do in a chemical spill|chemical leak|hazmat spill|toxic gas outside
column2: Go upwind, uphill; shelter inside if told.

column1: what do i do in a volcanic eruption|volcano eruption|volcano erupting|volcanic ash
column2: Evacuate if told; avoid ash, wear an N95.

column1: what do i do in a landslide|landslide|mudslide
column2: Get out of its path; if trapped, cover head.

column1: what do i do in a dust storm while driving|dust storm driving|haboob
column2: Pull off, lights off, foot off the brake.

column1: how do i survive a heat wave|heat wave|heat wave tips
column2: Stay cool indoors, drink water, check on others.

column1: what do i do if im trapped under rubble|trapped under rubble|trapped in a collapsed building
column2: Cover your mouth, tap on pipes, shout last.

column1: what do i do in an active shooter situation|active shooter|shooter what to do
column2: Run, hide, fight.

column1: how do i shut off the gas|gas shut off valve|how to turn off gas main
column2: Quarter turn so the valve crosses the pipe.

column1: how do i shut off the water main|water shut off|turn off water main
column2: Turn the main valve clockwise.
